message.content:
A cell that contains more than one nucleus is called a **multinucleated cell**.  
In many contexts it’s specifically referred to as a **syncytium** (a multinucleated syncytial cell) or, in the immune system, a **multinucleated giant cell**. These cells arise when several individual cells fuse together, resulting in a single cell with multiple nuclei.
